overview.overview:
Nebraska is projected to vote Republican in 2028, with an expected margin of about 15.5 points in the Republican direction. The state has backed the Republican presidential nominee by wide margins in recent cycles: Donald Trump carried it by about 19 points in 2020 and by about 20 points in 2024.

The forecast range runs from a Republican margin of about 6 points to one of about 25 points. Nebraska leans roughly 20 points more Republican than the nation as a whole, and its two electoral votes are not expected to decide the Electoral College. Statewide 2026 measures also point toward Republican strength.
overview.watch: A large national swing toward one party, or a shift in support among Nebraska voters tied to home-state candidates such as Don Bacon, could move the margin, though a change big enough to make the state competitive would be unusual.
key_factors: Nebraska's consistent Republican lean, with margins of roughly 19 and 20 points in the last two presidential elections
A national environment adjustment of 4.5 points, which narrows but does not close the state's Republican lean
Statewide 2026 Senate and governor measures that point toward Republican strength
